titolo: Strata: run a 125B model on a gaming PC, which size fits your RAM
descr: Strata is a free, open-source app that runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125-billion-parameter model that normally needs a server, on a home PC.
paragrafi: Strata is released under the MIT license, with no account and no telemetry. It chats, writes code and reads pictures, and your chats and files stay on your computer. The project on GitHub has passed 31,000 stars.
The rule is simple: you need at least 32 GB of RAM and graphics memory together. On a Mac or a Ryzen AI Max, that is the unified memory. You also need about 80 GB of free disk, better on an SSD.
Strata offers the same model in several sizes. With 32 GB, take Gyro-S, or the Coder for code. With 40 GB, Swift 1.5 or Gyro-M. With 48 GB, IQ3_XXS. With 64 GB, IQ3_S, the slowest and the best.

The project measured the speed on a 12 GB RTX 5070 with 64 GB of RAM. The Q2_0 size writes 94 tokens per second, IQ3_S writes 53, and the Coder writes 55. On a 16 GB AMD RX 9070 XT, the Coder writes 44 tokens per second.

To install it, download the app for your system and graphics card from the releases page on GitHub. On the first screen it reads your PC and recommends a size that fits. The model is a big download, about 40 to 70 GB.
perche: Coding agents like Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode can connect to Strata, because it speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs. Keep in mind that the speeds are the project's own measurements, and the Coder keeps half of the experts, so it is weaker outside code.
